sentences.text:
M/S. Ifcotokio General Insurance ... vs Smt. Gouni Bhagyamma,
on 19 June, 2023
Author: Lalitha Kanneganti

Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2525 of 2009
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the award dated 11.03.2008, in M.O.P.No.1349 of 2006 passed by the Chairman,
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - Principal District Judge, Ranga Reddy, L.B.Nagar, the Insurance Company has filed the present petition.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - Principal District Judge, Ranga Reddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Having heard Mr. K.S.N. Murthy, learned counsel for the appellant Insurance Company and Mr.
V.Atchuta Ram, learned counsel for claimants, perused the entire material on record.

3. The claim petition was filed by the claimants seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the death of the deceased that occurred on 29.09.2006 and the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.4,55,000/-.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the charge sheet itself was filed under Sections 3 and 181 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act') and the driver of the Motor vehicle was not having a valid driving license as on the date of accident.

It is also submitted that in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company 2 LK,J MACMA_2525_2009 Limited v. Swaran Singh and others1 case, the Tribunal ought to have applied the principle of pay and recover.

entities.text: National Insurance Company 2 LK,J MACMA_2525_2009 Limited v. Swaran Singh and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the Tribunal failed to consider the same and held that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

5. In this case, the appellant Insurance Company has failed to examine the owner of the vehicle,
except relying on the charge sheet and the evidence of RW-1.
Hence, Insurance Company has failed to discharge its burden.

6. As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court referred to supra, as the Insurance Company has failed to discharge the burden cast upon it, this Court is not inclined to entertain the appeal of the Insurance Company and apply the principle of pay and recover.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
